title: Tenant-responsive slab quotas with staggered rollup for reserved GPU pools
creator: Claire Wong
description:
Background: Customers on Reserved capacity have reported bursts that span our current daily/monthly reset boundaries, causing unexpected throttle regressions or invoice adjustments when usage crosses exact midnight UTC cutovers. The existing epoch-based resets were optimized for simplicity but surface two issues: 1) cross-tenant time zone mismatches leading to perceived double-consumption near cutovers, and 2) large legacy tenants with spiky patterns suffer high tail latency because our hard reset causes temporary contention on the quota service and ledger reconciliation subsystem.

Proposal summary: Implement a tenant-responsive slab-quota system with staggered rollups. Each tenant is assigned a soft quota slab aligned to their preferred anchoring (UTC or tenant-local-day). Instead of an instantaneous reset, slabs roll up in small staggered windows (e.g., 5–15 minutes per cohort) with an idempotent incremental refund/credit mechanism. This reduces contention, smooths billing anomalies, and permits a short reconciliation phase for late events. The system includes a configurable tenant cutoff policy (hard vs soft), a progressive reclaim timeline, and per-tenant telemetry to detect misalignment or abuse.

Goals: 1) Eliminate large spike in ledger corrections during cutover; 2) Reduce perceived double-charging around calendar boundaries; 3) Maintain deterministic metering guarantees for billing and rate-limiting; 4) Keep fail-safe hard reset path for emergency reconciliation.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change token accounting model, embedding units, or introduce new metering unit types. It focuses on reset/cutover behavior and reconciliation flow for reserved pools.
acceptance_criteria: Staggered rollup mechanism implemented and configurable per-tenant with default cohort size of 10 minutes
No more than 1% increase in median latency for quota check calls during tenant cutover windows compared to baseline
Billing ledger shows <0.5% increase in post-cutover correction entries for reserved customers in the first month
Household of test tenants (mix of small/large) demonstrate smooth throttle behavior around local-midnight in QA and canary
Can trigger emergency hard reset with idempotent rollback and documented operator runbook
tasks: Design: define slab size rules, cohort hashing, and tenant anchoring options (UTC, tenant-local-offset, business-hours)
API: extend quota config with "tenant_cutoff_policy", expose via Console and API for Dedicated customers
Runtime: implement staggered rollup worker with incremental ledger adjustments and idempotent checkpoints
Billing: adapt invoicing pipeline to consume reconciliation deltas and label corrective entries
Observability: add per-tenant cutover traces, rollup cohort metrics, and anomaly alerting
E2E: run canary with 50 reserved tenants across regions and verify behavior under synthetic midnight spikes
Runbook: create operator runbook for emergency hard reset and reconciliation monitoring
implementation_notes: Choose a deterministic cohorting hash based on tenant_id % N to ensure stable staggering across restarts
Rollup worker should emit small batched refund entries to ledger (max 500 tenants per batch) to avoid DB hot partitions
Use optimistic idempotency tokens on ledger writes to avoid double-applies from retries
Introduce a reconciliation window (default 48 hours) for late events; these are tagged as 'recon.delta' in billing exports
For tenants with hard cutoff=true, perform a tight finalization step at T+1 minute with operator approval recorded
Keep a metrics-only dry-run in prod for two weeks before enabling automatic credits for customers with >$10k monthly commits
telemetry_and_alerting: quota.cutover.latency P50/P95 during each cohort window
alert if cohort worker error rate > 0.5% for >10 minutes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (design + tests): implement feature flags and unit/integ tests in canary environment
Phase 2 (dry-run): enable metrics-only cohorting in prod for two weeks - monitor telemetry
Phase 3 (canary credits): enable automatic incremental credits for a small reserved tenant cohort (50 tenants)
Phase 4 (wider roll): expand to all Reserved customers with gradual cohort size tuning
Phase 5 (post-mortem): run 30/60/90 day checks and publish runbook update
